name: Pioneer 11 Mission
text: · 0 credits. Mission: the first time you visit Jupiter, and the first time you visit Saturn, cover that reward. Playing it is still your main action even at 0 credits. A probe already on the planet when you play the card doesn’t count — move onto it again; orbiters and landers never count as visits.

name: Mariner 10 Mission
text: · 0 credits. Same as Pioneer 11, for Venus and Mercury.

name: Voyager 2 Mission
text: · 0 credits. Same as Pioneer 11, for Uranus and Neptune.

name: Galileo Mission
text: · 0 credits. Same as Pioneer 11, for Venus and Jupiter.

name: Servicing Mission
text: — move first, then check for a probe next to Earth.

name: Twin Probes
text: — mission: two probes in space at once, each on a different planet (not Earth; orbiters and landers don’t count).

name: Quantum Data Storage
text: — counts the data in your data pool only, not in your computer.

name: Falcon Heavy
text: · 3 credits. Launch two probes (plus the printed publicity); these two launches ignore your probe limit, so you can end up with 3 or 4 probes in space. Your normal launches still respect the limit afterwards.

name: First Human in Space
text: — publicity stops at 10; any excess is lost.

name: Grant
text: · 1 credit. Draw a card (from the row or blind from the deck), reveal it and gain its free-action corner (top left). A blind draw risks a corner you can’t use.

name: Two-planet Flyby Maneuver
text: — two different planets you move onto this turn; the one you start on counts only if you leave and come back, and lasts through later free-action moves.

name: James Clerk Maxwell Telescope
text: — a Scan without the base cost (purple-tech extras still cost); its signal token arrives after the Scan, too late to use in it.

name: Atmospheric Entry
text: · 1 credit. Remove one of your orbiters from any planet for the printed points, data and card. The emptied orbit space frees up: if it was the first space, the next orbiter there gains its 3 points again (others don’t slide).

name: Dragonfly
text: · 1 credit. Land, even on a space already taken, and still gain the covered reward (the first-lander data). Works on an occupied moon if you have the moon tech.

name: OSIRIS-REx
text: · 1 credit. Choose one of your probes: data if it sits on asteroids, plus 1 data per orthogonally adjacent asteroid space. The probe doesn’t have to be on asteroids itself.

name: Contracted Research
text: — playable at 0 publicity and still gives the tech (the best way to play it).

name: Gravitational Slingshot
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; each time you visit a planet this turn you may take a move instead of the publicity. Lasts the whole turn, free-action moves included; the planet you start on doesn’t count.

name: Mercury Flyby
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; if you visit Mercury this turn, gain the printed points — once, however many visits.

name: Venus Flyby
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; points for visiting Venus this turn, once.

name: Mars Flyby
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; points for visiting Mars this turn, once.

name: Jupiter Flyby
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; points for visiting Jupiter this turn, once.

name: Saturn Flyby
text: · 2 credits. Three moves; points for visiting Saturn this turn, once.

name: Lightsail
text: · 2 credits. Four moves; 1 point for each different planet you visit this turn, Earth included (the same planet twice still counts once).

name: Through the Asteroid Belt
text: · 1 credit. Two moves, and leaving asteroids costs only 1 move this turn (as with the orange asteroid tech).

name: Hubble Space Telescope
text: · 1 credit. One move, then mark a signal in a sector with one of your probes. Move first; the probe must be on the Solar system board, not an orbiter or lander.

name: Kepler Space Telescope
text: · 2 credits. As Hubble, but both signals go in the same sector with that probe.

name: James Webb Space Telescope
text: · 2 credits. Mark three signals: one in the probe’s sector and one in each neighbouring sector.

name: Great Observatories Project
text: · 2 credits. Choose up to 3 probes on the Solar system board — yours or other players’ — and mark a signal in each one’s sector.

name: MUREP Idea Competition
text: — you still gain 1 publicity and 2 random cards with an empty hand.

name: Delayed Launch
text: — triggers as you pass, so the launched probe can’t move until next round; at your probe limit, mark the mission without launching.

name: Private Sector Investment
text: — first an income increase (tuck a card, gain its resource now), then 1 random card per tech of your most numerous tech colour.

name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
text: — data in your pool and in your computer both count.

name: Pandora Satellite
text: — main actions at 0 credits; signals in your probe’s sector(s) give no data (return it to the supply).

name: Space Rendezvous
text: — move first, then check for a shared space with any probe (yours or another player’s).

name: LOFAR Array
text: — a Scan without the base cost; needs every one of the 8 sectors won or holding your signal.

name: Allen Telescope Array
text: · 2 credits. Discard two cards from the card row for their signals (refill only after both); if you complete a sector this turn, gain the printed move.

name: ALMA Observatory
text: · 2 credits. As Allen, with the printed reward for completing a sector this turn.

name: Very Large Array
text: · 2 credits. As Allen, with the printed reward for completing a sector this turn. Both row cards are discarded before the row refills.

name: Square Kilometre Array
text: · 3 credits. Discard all three row cards for their signals, then refill; 2 points per different sector you marked — up to 6.

name: Lovell Telescope
text: · 3 credits. A Scan action without its base cost (purple-tech extras still cost). Mission: once you have at least 8 publicity, take the reward.

name: Parkes Observatory
text: · 2 credits. A Scan without the base cost; 2 points per red-sector signal you mark with it.

name: Deep Synoptic Array
text: · 2 credits. A Scan without the base cost; 2 points per yellow-sector signal you mark with it.

name: VERITAS Telescopes
text: · 2 credits. A Scan without the base cost; 2 points per blue-sector signal you mark with it.

name: Arecibo Observatory
text: · 3 credits. A Scan without the base cost, plus one extra signal in any sector.

name: Uranus Orbiter and Probe
text: · 2 credits. Launch. Mission: an orbiter or lander at Uranus — its moon counts too (CGE: missing from the card text, always intended).

name: Trident Probe
text: · 2 credits. Launch. Mission: an orbiter or lander at Neptune — its moon counts too (CGE ruling).

name: FAST Telescope Construction
text: · 4 credits. Two row signals (discard, then refill the row), then rotate and take a telescope tech — in that order, so a card from the tech’s bonus comes from the refilled row..

name: Yevpatoria Telescope Construction
text: · 3 credits. Publicity, rotate and take a telescope tech, then you may discard 1 card from your hand for its signal (sector = the card’s top-right colour)..

name: Clean Space Initiative
text: · 1 credit. Discard all three row cards and use their free-action corners; they’re discarded even when you can’t or don’t want to use a corner.

name: Pre-launch Testing
text: · 2 credits. Launch; 1 move per card with a move free-action corner that you show from your hand.

name: SETI Institute
text: · 2 credits. Mission with three rewards: cover one each time you scan in the right way, any order — one per triggering action.

name: ISS
text: · 2 credits. Mission with three rewards, one per triggering launch, any order.

name: Cape Canaveral SFS
text: · 1 credit. Mission with three rewards, one per triggering launch, any order.

name: International Collaboration
text: · 2 credits. Take a tech another player already has — no rotation and no printed tile bonus, but the free launch or 2 data of those two techs still apply.

name: Sample Return
text: · 1 credit. Remove one of your landers from a planet or moon to mark a trace. A freed first space gives its 2 data again to the next lander.

name: Chandra Space Observatory
text: · 2 credits. Two signals in a sector with your probe. Mission: signals in 4 different sectors — counted on the board when you complete it; you may complete it before the sector you just filled resolves.

name: NIAC Program
text: · 2 credits. Draw 3 cards (shown as “3?”). Mission: no cards in hand — Exertian cards don’t count as in hand.

name: Fusion Reactor
text: · 3 credits. The printed reward per card you have tucked for energy income, then tuck this card (an income increase: gain its resource now).

name: NASA Image of the Day
text: · 3 credits. Publicity, the printed reward per card tucked for card income, then tuck this card for income.

name: Government Funding
text: · 3 credits. The printed reward per card tucked for credit income, then tuck this one too — count first, tuck after.

name: Coronal Spectrograph
text: · 1 credit. Mark a purple trace for a species where you already have a yellow one (discovery and overflow spaces count as that species’).

name: Electron Microscope
text: · 1 credit. Mark a yellow trace for a species where you already have a blue one.

name: Exascale Supercomputer
text: · 1 credit. Mark a blue trace for a species where you already have a purple one.

name: Telescope Time Allocation
text: · 2 credits. Mission: one reward per Scan, any order. If the Scan completes a sector you may cover a reward first and use its extra signal before the sector resolves.

name: Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope
text: · 3 credits. Rotate and take a telescope tech. Mission: win the same sector twice..

name: Strategic Planning
text: · 1 credit. Mission: when you pay 1, 2 or 3 credits to play a card as your main action, cover the matching reward. Discarding a card doesn’t trigger it.

name: First Black Hole Photo
text: · 2 credits. Mark a blue trace. Mission: one reward per later blue trace, any order.

name: Planetary Geologic Mapping
text: · 3 credits. Rotate and take a probe tech. Mission: an orbiter and a lander at the same planet — a lander on its moon counts (CGE ruling)..

name: Solvay Conference
text: · 2 credits. End-of-game: score the gold tile you didn’t mark at its lowest (rightmost) tier; if you marked fewer than 3, pick one of the unmarked.

name: Planet Hunters
text: · 1 credit. Draw a card, then discard up to 3 cards from your hand for their signals.

name: Control Center
text: · 1 credit. Mission: when you mark a signal in a yellow, red or blue sector, cover that colour’s reward. One Scan can trigger several; older signals don’t.

name: Lunar Gateway
text: · 3 credits. Land, even on a moon without the tech. Mission: one reward per later orbit or landing, any order.

name: PLATO
text: · 1 credit. Three signals in a sector with your probe, but return their data to the supply — good for excess signals.

name: PIXL
text: · 3 credits. Rotate and take a computer tech, then 1 point per publicity you have. You may place data mid-action to gain publicity first..

name: Orbiting Lagrange Point
text: · 1 credit. A signal in a sector with your probe; if it’s your only signal there (none before), the card returns to your hand — even if the signal completes the sector.

name: Amateur Astronomers
text: · 2 credits. Three times, one by one: discard the deck’s top card for its signal. Mandatory, even if it helps others.

name: Asteroids Flyby
text: · 0 credits. One move; data for visiting asteroids this turn, once. A main action despite costing 0.

name: Cometary Encounter
text: · 1 credit. Two moves; points for visiting a comet this turn, once.

name: Trajectory Correction
text: · 1 credit. One move; points and publicity if you move within the same ring (same distance from the Sun) this turn.

name: Euclid Telescope Construction
text: · 3 credits. Take an orange or a purple tech (one rotation either way). End-of-game: points per matching item, as printed.

name: NEAR Shoemaker
text: · 1 credit. Publicity now; end-of-game 13 points only if one of your probes is on asteroids when the game ends — a rotation after you pass can push it off.

name: Advanced Navigation System
text: · 1 credit. Mission: each visit to a planet other than Earth covers one reward; revisiting the same planet counts again.

name: Asteroid Research
text: · 0 credits. Mission: each time you visit asteroids on your turn, cover one reward — a rotation on your turn that pushes your probe onto asteroids counts.

name: Optimal Launch Window
text: · 2 credits. Launch, then 1 move per other planet or comet lined up with Earth outward from the Sun (up to 3).

name: Herschel Space Observatory
text: · 1 credit. A signal in a sector with your probe. Mission: signals in 4 different sectors, counted on the board.

name: Noto Radio Observatory
text: · 2 credits. A Scan without the base cost (purple-tech extras still cost), plus publicity.

name: Algonquin Radio Observatory
text: · 1 credit. A signal in each of the four colours’ sectors, but no data from them.

name: Cornell University
text: · 1 credit. Mission: when you discard a card from your hand for its free-action corner, cover the reward matching that corner (publicity, data or move); stronger alien corners count if they include it.
